modes.name: verbose_reply
modes.definition: The reply contains content the request did not need: data recaps, repeated sentences, a recap turn before the needed question, or closing filler. For merchant and support sessions, extra order data is acceptable because it saves a follow-up lookup; filler, apologies and repeated sentences still count.
modes.boundary: Extra tool calls belong to redundant_tool_call; markup belongs to formatting_noise.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-7 (HW4 revision to SPEC.md); loosely RESP-5
modes.revision_note: Reviewer rule from the 10% audit: extra data is fine for merchant/support sessions (it saves a tool call); filler, apologies and repeats still count.

modes.name: redundant_tool_call
modes.definition: A tool call whose answer the agent already has, or that the request did not need.
modes.boundary: A call that errors belongs to rejected_tool_argument.

modes.name: internal_policy_id_shown
modes.definition: The reply shows an internal policy identifier (for example cw-refunds) to the user.
modes.boundary: Naming the policy by its plain-language title is the wanted form and is not this mode.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-1 (revised in HW4: cite by plain-language title, never by internal identifier)
modes.revision_note: Negatives are rare: 98 of about 102 policy replies show an ID. #46 (confirmed) states the $100 rule in plain words; #71 and #72 are dispute-ticket confirmations with no ID.

modes.name: rejected_tool_argument
modes.definition: An agent-supplied tool argument is in a form the tool rejects (not_found or invalid_argument), for example a numeric store id where a store name is required.
modes.boundary: A permission denial is expected behavior, not this mode.
modes.revision_note: Rare: 4 of 250 traces, all the same merchant (store id 1 passed where a store name is required). Reviewer: the agent should map the current merchant to the store name; the prompt gives the id but not the name.

modes.name: unprofessional_style
modes.definition: The reply uses markup or tone that reads as unprofessional: double asterisks, pipe tables, emoji, an inconsistent label/date layout, or an apologetic, gushing or falsely personal tone.
modes.boundary: Length and repetition belong to verbose_reply; showing an internal policy ID belongs to internal_policy_id_shown.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-6 (HW4 revision to SPEC.md); loosely RESP-5
modes.revision_note: Merged from formatting_noise and tone_off to stay within the 8-mode cap. One product change (a plain, professional style instruction in the prompt) would fix both. Earlier the reviewer had chosen to keep them separate; the cap and the merge rule reversed that.

modes.name: missing_data_not_flagged
modes.definition: The record itself shows missing or inconsistent data (a null date, or dates that contradict each other) and the reply does not say so.
modes.boundary: How the agent explains things belongs to other modes.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 (clarified in HW4 with null and contradictory date examples)
modes.revision_note: Narrowed after Workshop review: the agent has no tool to look up a product by ID, so a store/product mismatch (order 8003, #51 and #23) is not visible from the record alone. Needs 2+ more positives from the batch 3 depth search. Then extended to contradictory dates (reviewer decision) and grown to 6 positives from the batch 3 depth search.

modes.name: persona_not_clarified
modes.definition: The caller sounds like they are acting in a different capacity than their session role, and the agent takes a consequential action (such as issuing a refund) or answers in the wrong capacity without asking which capacity it is serving.
modes.boundary: A refusal that leaks information belongs to RESP-4.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-9 (HW4 revision to SPEC.md); SPEC Section 3 (roles and permissions)
modes.revision_note: Reviewer rule: it counts when a consequential action is taken on a guess about the capacity, not for a lucky guess with no action. #24, #44, #46 and the Workshop run 14aef58b were confirmed under the older wording and must be re-checked against this rule.

modes.name: reply_misses_the_ask
modes.definition: The reply does not directly answer the question asked, or leaves out information the person needs to act on it (for example the reason and time limit for a dispute, a plain yes on a cancellation, or a clear way to tell duplicate listings apart).
modes.boundary: Extra or repeated wording belongs to verbose_reply; missing or inconsistent record data belongs to missing_data_not_flagged.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-8 (HW4 revision to SPEC.md); loosely RESP-5
modes.revision_note: Taxonomy revision: began as dispute_basis_not_explained (candidate from reviewer note on #71). In the final 15 batch, #92 and #94 showed the same underlying problem, so the mode was broadened rather than adding a 9th. One product change (answer the question asked and include what the person needs) corrects all three. Close negatives (proposed, unconfirmed): #28 and #38.
